{{c|''Appearing againe in Galilee, where Peter was fishing with his fellowes: and causing them after they had al night taken none, to catch a great multitude, which Peter draweth to land, where he also dineth them: 15 He (expressing what this fishing signified) maketh Peter his Vicar, committing vnto him the feeding of his lambes and sheepe: 18 and reuealeth vnto him, that he also shal be crucified, to the glorie of God, 20 admonishing him to minde that, rather then to be curious about Iohns death.''}} {{dropinitial|A|image=Rhemes New Testament 1582 initial A, a bearded man.png|imgsize=115px|fl={{verse|chapter=21|verse=1}}}}FTER {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel on wenseday in Easter weeke.}}{{sc|Iesvs}} manifested him self againe at the sea of Tibérias. And he manifested thus: {{verse|chapter=21|verse=2}}† There vvere together Simon Peter and Thomas vvho is called Didymus, and Nathanael vvhich vvas of Cana in Galilee, and the sonnes of Zebedee, and tvvo others of his disciples. {{verse|chapter=21|verse=3}}† Simon Peter saith to them, I goe to fish. They say to him, VVe also come vvith thee. And they vvent forth and got vp into the boate: and that night they tooke nothing. {{verse|chapter=21|verse=4}}† But vvhen morning vvas novv come, {{sc|Iesvs}} stoode on the shore: yet the disciples knevv not that it was {{sc|Iesvs}}. {{verse|chapter=21|verse=5}}† {{sc|Iesvs}} therfore saith to them, Children, haue you any meate? They ansvvered him, No. {{verse|chapter=21|verse=6}}† He saith to them, Cast the nette on the right side of the boate: and you shal finde. They therfore did cast it: and novv they vvere not able to dravv it for the multitude of fishes. {{verse|chapter=21|verse=7}}† That disciple therfore vvhom {{sc|Iesvs}} loued, saith to Peter, It is our Lord. {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ See in S. Augustine ''tract. 122 in Io''. the great mysterie hereof concerning the CHVRCH, and in S. Gregorie ''hom. 24 in Euang''. and S. Bernard ''li. 2 c. 8 de consid''. Peters PRIMACIE here mistically signified.}}∷ Simon Peter when he had heard that it is our Lord: girded his coate vnto him (for he vvas naked) and cast him self into the sea. {{verse|chapter=21|verse=8}}† But the other disciples came in the boate (for they vvere not farre from the land, but as it vvere tvvo hundred cubits) dravving the nette of fishes. {{verse|chapter=21|verse=9}}† Therefore after they came dovvne to land, they savv hote coles lying, and fish laid thereon, and bread. {{verse|chapter=21|verse=10}}† {{sc|Iesvs}} saith to them, Bring hither of the fishes that you tooke novv. {{verse|chapter=21|verse=11}}† Simon Peter vvent vp, and drevv the nette to the land, ful of great fishes, an hundred fiftie three. And although they vvere so many, the nette vvas not broken. {{verse|chapter=21|verse=12}}† {{sc|Iesvs}} saith to them, Come, dine. And none of them that sate at meate, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ ''the disciples,''}}∷ durst aske him, Who art thou? knovving that it is our Lord. {{verse|chapter=21|verse=13}}† And {{sc|Iesvs}} commeth and taketh the bread and giueth them, and the fish in like maner. {{verse|chapter=21|verse=14}}† This novv the {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ Not the third apparition, but the third day of his apparitions. for he appeared in the very day of his Resurrection often, againe vpon Low Sunday, then this third time, And S. Marke saying, ''last he appeared, c. 16, 14'': meaneth his last apparition the first day.}}∷ third time {{sc|Iesvs}} vvas manifested to his disciples, after he vvas risen from the dead.

{{verse|chapter=21|verse=15}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel on the eue of SS. Peter and Paul.}}Therfore vvhen they had dined, {{sc|Iesvs}} saith to Simon<noinclude>{{rh|||Peter,}}</noinclude>
